original_question: Which gene, located on the short arm of the X chromosome and encoding a protein implicated in controlling cell growth and differentiation, is associated with mutations that cause a disease described independently by its namesake doctors in 1966 and 1971 respectively?

final_qi.question: Which gene, located on the short arm of the X chromosome and encoding a protein implicated in controlling cell growth and differentiation, is associated with mutations that cause a disease described independently by its namesake doctors in 1966 and 1971 respectively?
final_qi.long_answer: RPS6KA3 lies on Xp22.2-p22.1 and encodes the serine/threonine kinase RSK2, a component of the MAPK/ERK pathway that modulates cell growth and differentiation. Pathogenic mutations in RPS6KA3 give rise to Coffin–Lowry syndrome, a disorder first reported by Dr. G. S. Coffin in 1966 and independently by Dr. R. B. Lowry in 1971.

final_answer.long_answer: Mutations in the RPS6KA3 gene, mapped to Xp22.2 on the short arm of the X chromosome, cause Coffin-Lowry syndrome. RPS6KA3 encodes the serine/threonine kinase RSK2, a component of the MAPK signalling cascade that regulates cell growth and differentiation. Coffin (1966) and Lowry (1971) independently described the characteristic clinical picture, and the disorder now bears their names.
